about: Ceilings for `check-editor-performance.py --budgets`: medians of a headless run, per action. Time ceilings are about 2.5x what a quiet machine measures, because machines differ; allocation ceilings are about 25% over the measured value, because allocation depends on the code and not on the machine. After a deliberate change, re-measure with `--budgets --measure` and lower or raise the number with the reason in the commit. Measured 2026-10-01: tab switch 1.0-1.5 ms and 132-203 KiB, interaction 0.9-1.7 ms, selection 2.3 ms. Tab-switch allocation re-baselined 2026-10-29 to 249-291 KiB (after the same day's allocation work: hashed cache keys, shared style storage and identity arrays, lazy tooltip content and layout-node text styles, shared enum constants, shared decoded geometry): since 2026-10-01 the app grew from 9 to 14 dock panels (mission panel, machine axis travel controls, project configurations, inspection camera), every switch walks the tab chrome of all of them, and the per-node cost fell meanwhile (a RenderNode was 936 bytes, now 288). How much of the rise comes from the extra panels, and how much from a code change, is not attributed to commits. Re-baselined 2026-10-30 after retention work (toolbar keyed on what it shows, in-place restyle, patch frames): tab switch 136-174 KiB. Interaction allocation is the UI's own, from input to the end of the frame (interaction.json), and has a floor of 4 KiB so that actions allocating nearly nothing are not failed by noise. CNC retention and composite updater ownership measured 2026-10-30 reduce hierarchy-to-sensors exact action allocation by 3704 bytes, so its ceiling falls from 217 to 214 KiB. Tabs and popup reconciliation measured 2026-10-31 reduce hierarchy-to-sensors exact allocation by another 240 bytes through dependency snapshot and state-handle reuse; its ceiling falls from 214 to 213.8 KiB. An action's own entry replaces the "*" one, so it repeats the time ceiling.
